title: Geometry-induced flocking and topological sound on a defect-free curved surface
authors: Devendra Saini, Atanu Bhatta, Pritha Dolai
abstract: We study an ordered polar active flock on a torus and show that topological sound persists on a compact curved surface without topological defects or physical boundaries. Using the covariant Toner Tu theory, we derive an effective nonHermitian Dirac operator whose curvature-induced mass changes sign across the outer and inner equators, producing two Jackiw Rebbi domain walls. These support co-propagating but distinct chiral edge excitations: a density mode localized on the positively curved outer equator and a Goldstone mode localized on the negatively curved inner equator. The bulk bands possess opposite half-integer Chern numbers whose jumps across the domain walls are determined by the sign of the Gaussian curvature. We further show that the localised modes are protected by a one-dimensional Callias index theorem, while the sum of the local indices obeys the Poincare Hopf theorem on the compact surface. Our results establish that curvature alone, independent of defects and boundaries, is sufficient to generate and protect topological sound in active matter, providing a unified connection between non-Hermitian topology, differential geometry, and hydrodynamic theory of collective motion.
summary: This paper investigates how geometric curvature influences collective motion in active matter flocks on a curved surface like a torus. By deriving an effective non-Hermitian Dirac operator, the authors show that the curvature itself generates protected, chiral sound modes at the equator, even without defects. This establishes a fundamental link between differential geometry and the hydrodynamics of active systems.
main_problem: To determine if topological sound in active matter flocking on a curved surface is a consequence of local geometry, independent of defects and physical boundaries.
main_result: Curvature alone is sufficient to generate and protect topological sound in active matter, evidenced by protected chiral edge excitations localized on the outer and inner equators of the torus.
method: The authors use the covariant Toner-Tu theory, linearizing the equations to derive an effective non-Hermitian Dirac operator whose topological properties are analyzed using index theorems.
model_or_system: The system is an ordered polar active flock studied on a torus (a compact, curved surface). The analysis focuses on the collective excitations derived from the linearized hydrodynamic equations.
key_observables: Chiral edge excitations (density mode and Goldstone mode), Chern numbers, and the index of the Dirac operator.
important_parameters: The aspect ratio ($\epsilon = R/r$) of the torus acts as a control parameter; the Gaussian curvature ($K_G$) dictates the sign of the topological change.
main_assumptions: Viscous terms are neglected in the steady state calculation, and the analysis is performed in the vicinity of the equators where the mass term is small.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the steady state density profile on a torus; Figure 2 shows the normalized steady state density variation with the aspect ratio $\epsilon$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context by contrasting the torus with other surfaces, derives the steady state, linearizes the equations to obtain a Dirac Hamiltonian, and then analyzes the resulting topological edge states using Callias and Poincaré-Hopf index theorems.
why_interesting: The work provides a deep connection between continuum geometry (curvature), topological invariants (Chern/Callias indices), and the collective dynamics of active matter, which has parallels in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
